indicator-camouflaged-by-resting-style-o: Every control already has a border that looks just like the focus outline, so when one gets keyboard focus the highlight blends in invisibly.
indicator-below-perception-threshold: The focus highlight technically appears but is so thin, faint, or low-contrast that a keyboard user can't actually see which element has focus.
script-removes-focus-on-receipt: JavaScript yanks focus away the instant a control receives it, so the focus highlight never appears and keyboard users can't tell where they are on the page.
pointer-only-feedback-masquerading-as-fo: Controls only light up on mouse hover and the keyboard outline is stripped, so a keyboard user tabbing through sees no sign of which element is focused.
drawn-indicator-fails-forced-colors-or-a: A custom focus highlight (a box-shadow or painted square) looks fine normally but vanishes in Windows high-contrast mode or can't be located by screen-reader users.
indicator-clipped-or-scrolled-out-of-vis: The focus outline is drawn but gets clipped by an overflow container, hidden behind a sticky header, or scrolled off-screen, so the keyboard user never sees it.
